newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says Commission must notify Social Fund recipients.
newsitem.headline: Court says Commission must notify Social Fund recipients.

text.p: The European Court of Justice confirmed an earlier ruling from the Court of First Instance that recipients of European Social Funds must be notified directly if the European Commission seeks a refund of monies.
The Commission appealed the earlier decision (T-450/93) which found their failure to give notice to fund recipients before seeking a refund prevented the opportunity for a proper defence.

"The Commission decision deprived the respondents of the whole of the assistance which had initally been granted to them. They therefore directly suffered the economic consequences of the decision...," the court said.

The court affirmed the earlier ruling that fund recipients are directly and individually concerned when the Commission tries to cut or retake the funding, and therefore have a right to bring a claim and receive notice of the Commission's reasons.
The Commission erred when it directed its communication only to the portuguese Ministry of Employment and Social Security (DAFSE), and not the individual companies.

In 1987, the European Commission approved 630,642,227, escudos, half of which was to be paid by the European Social Fund for remedial training funds to high school graduates. The Fund made a 50 percent payment that same year.
When the portuguese beneficiaries submitted a claim in 1988 for further funding, the Fund reviewed expenditures and decided some of the monies had been used for ineligible expenditures.
The Commission asked the Portuguese to refund ESC 138,271,804.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: portuguese)
"European Social Fund - Decision reducing financial assistance initially granted - Infringement of the rights of the defence - Right of interested parties to be heard"
Commission of the European Communities, appellant

appeal against the Judgment of the Court of First Instance of the European Communities in Case T-450/93 Lisrestal and Others v Commission (1994) ECR II-1177, seeking to have that judgment set aside in part,
2. Orders the appellant to pay the costs.
